tip: Hindi has no verb for 'have'. नरेश के पास (Naresh ke paas) is literally 'near Naresh' – so 'Naresh has 500 rupees' comes out as 'near Naresh are 500 rupees'.
With pronouns, के fuses in: आपके पास (aapke paas) = 'you have' – one word आपके (aapke), never आप के (aap ke). Same fusion in मेरे (mere) and उसके (uske).
Position words follow the noun in Hindi: दीवार के पीछे (deewaar ke peechhe) is 'the wall behind' – the reverse of English 'behind the wall'.
Nouns ending in -आ shift to -ए before position words: दरवाज़ा (darvaaza = door) becomes दरवाज़े के अंदर (darvaaze ke andar = inside the doorway).
कौन (kaun = who) and क्या (kya = what) both become किस (kis) before a position word: किस गली में (kis galee mein = in which lane).
के ऊपर (ke oopar) alone means sitting on top. Motion across adds से (se): पुल के ऊपर से गुज़रती है (pul ke oopar se guzarti hai) = passes over the bridge.
बिना (bina = without) wraps its noun: बिना छाते के (bina chhaate ke = without an umbrella) – bina goes before the noun, ke comes after.
'Instead of' is की जगह (kee jagah), literally 'at the place of': बिरयानी की जगह पुलाव (biryaanee kee jagah pulaav) = pulao in biryani's place.
के हिसाब से (ke hisaab se) = 'according to', literally 'by the account of': नक्शे के हिसाब से (nakshe ke hisaab se) = going by the map.
A verb before के लिए (ke lie = for) takes the -ने form: जाना (jaana = to go) becomes जाने (jaane): स्टेशन जाने के लिए (station jaane ke lie) = to get to the station.
'Wait for me' is मेरा इंतज़ार करना (mera intazaar karna) – literally 'do my waiting'. Hindi says whose waiting it is, not who you wait for.
'About' is three words: के बारे में (ke baare mein), literally 'in the matter of': पैसे के बारे में (paise ke baare mein) = about money.
बीचोबीच (beechobeech) is बीच (beech = middle) doubled: पुणे के बीचोबीच (Pune ke beechobeech) = right in the center of Pune. Doubling adds the 'exactly'.
Tiny ही (hee) means 'right/exactly': ऑफ़िस के सामने ही (office ke saamne hee) = right in front of the office, that exact spot.
से (se) usually means 'from', but with motion it can be 'through': दरवाज़े से गुज़रकर (darvaaze se guzarkar) = passing through the doorway.
An instruction can be just the -ना form: मुड़ जाना (mud jaana) = 'turn' as a gentle command, softer than the direct मुड़ो (mudo). Common in directions.
